checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: Vertical ~10s reel with all five photos in order
must.why: The video is 9:16 and 10.1 s. Storefront, latte, barista and interior show in order. The pastries photo is only seen as a blend in the 4.1 s frame, which is a transition.

must.item: Each caption appears exactly with its photo
must.why: 'Stay a shile' appears instead of 'Stay a while' in the video. The pastries source frame reads 'Something sweeet'. The video frames I sampled never show a clean 'Something sweet'.

must.item: Captions visible long enough and not clipped
must.why: The captions I could see are inside the frame. Only four frames were sampled, and the pastries caption never showed up clearly. Timing cannot be confirmed.

must.item: Caption contrast and placement legible over every photo
must.why: The captions are white with a dark outline on a dark band. They are readable in every frame I saw, though the band is semi-transparent. During the 4.1 s dissolve the busy double exposure makes the text harder to read.
The file has an audio track with a peak of -2.1 dB, but I can't judge the mood.

exact_text.read_as: Something sweeet (in the captioned frame; not clearly visible in the video)

faults.what: The final caption reads 'Stay a shile' instead of 'Stay a while'. The error is in the captioned frame and carries into the video.
The pastries frame reads 'Something sweeet', which has an extra 'e'. The pastries photo is not clearly seen in the video samples.
The 4.1 s frame is a messy double exposure of latte, pastries and café. It has a circular warp, and the caption overlays a muddled image.
The photos were reframed or extended into vertical format. The storefront shows extra street, and the barista is changed with a new foreground cup. This alters the originals.

summary: A 10 s vertical reel with legible captions came out, but 'Stay a while' is misspelled as 'Stay a shile', 'Something sweet' has a typo in its frame, and the transitions are messy.
